profile_text.body:
EleutherAI is a nonprofit organization, listed with a remote headquarters and the website eleuther.ai. Its site describes research aimed at technical problems in frontier AI systems rather than at commercial products.

Two research threads are described on the site. The first is eliciting latent knowledge, or ELK, inside a model's activations, which the organization says it pursues because humans will not always be able to independently check whether a model's claims are true or false. The second concerns test set contamination in generative evaluations. In that work, the organization reports pretraining language models on mixtures of web data and the MATH benchmark, sweeping model sizes and the number of test set replicas in the pretraining corpus, and finding that performance improves with contamination and model size. Using scaling laws, it reports that including even a single test set replica lets models reach a lower result, a finding it describes as surprising.

The record holds no products, no MCP servers, and no litigation involving the company.
